spec.title: PROP-020: Named local workspace pairs and checkout writers

status.comment: checkout writer capability; named pair lifecycle remains open

p.PATCHSET-WRITER: Every acquireLock writing scope owns a physical patchset checkout guard in addition to its legacy per-tree generation. Different fork tree IDs, aliases and separate command scopes in the same process cannot overlap one checkout. A nested scope borrows only an active issued parent capability for the same physical checkout; copying metadata or a handle, reusing a released handle or supplying a foreign parent refuses. The checkout guard survives until all parent/child references release. Partial acquisitions unwind. Existing live legacy tree owners refuse; unknown foreign owners and non-regular lock files fail closed. The requested tree generation retains its established stale recovery protocol. This is cooperative exclusion for participating writers and detection of already live legacy owners, not a claim to control arbitrary uncooperative programs starting afterward. Per-tree lock bytes and atomic hard-link/generation ownership remain unchanged.

p.WORKSPACE-REGISTRY: The user-controlled workspaces.json carries codkitWorkspaceRegistry:1, monotonically revised under an exclusive contained registry lock with byte comparison before updates. Strict pair records bind UUID/name/state, original repository/common-directory, checkout path/task branch/base commit, type declaration digest/contract, pin and owner/session timestamps. UUID and case-insensitive name collisions, overlapping nonremoved checkout roots, shared pair roots and mismatched UUID task branch/pin refuse. UUID derives operational ref prefixes without rewriting source config. Checkout receipts use codkitWorkspaceCheckout:1, binding ID, role, common directory and base commit. Named resolution and lifecycle transitions remain pending; registry data alone never authorizes foreign cleanup.

p.WORKSPACE-CREATE: Create reserves a creating journal before Git mutations, creates a task-branch patchset worktree and detached fork worktree at the selected immutable config/pin, and records active only after actual Git registration/branch and contained checkout receipts are verified. Source repositories, Git administration, registry and pair directory are disjoint. Owner/session may retry only the same recorded creating pair; changed partial checkout, foreign receipts, namespace/name conflicts or directory aliases refuse without cleanup or overwrite. Partial failure leaves journal/resources reviewable rather than promising rollback. Public CLI/selection, finish/remove and full phase acceptance remain pending.

p.WORKSPACE-FINISH: Finish verifies both actual registered checkout identities and immutable role receipts while holding checkout writer capabilities. It refuses dirty/untracked task work, moved or missing custody, unextracted detached history, stale generated cache/mark/fingerprint, own/upstream drift and active/unresolved daemons. An untouched detached baseline can finish without fabricated apply evidence. A finished record preserves patchset/fork immutable heads and optional delta fingerprint with timestamp; finished/removing/removed states require that proof. Marked generated fork branches must belong to the workspace UUID namespace. Finish preserves both checkout directories; deletion/cleanup remains a separate action and integration is still pending.

p.WORKSPACE-PAIR-LIFECYCLE: A named workspace is a local patchset task worktree and fork worktree pair with stable UUID, type/pin, ref namespace and owner/session metadata. Create/list/show/finish/remove operate on validated real Git worktrees. Generated refs include workspace UUID. Named launcher resolution supplies where roots and refuses conflicting root flags. Finish proves save/clean and no live writers/daemons before cleanup; removal never destroys dirty, foreign or unowned roots. Without named selection legacy root/ref behavior remains compatible.

p.WORKSPACE-REMOVE: Removal requires a finished proof and both unchanged recorded heads. While holding checkout writer capabilities it checks actual Git registration, exact role receipts, daemon state, Git cleanliness and a physical inventory including ignored files and empty directories. Only tracked files and validated Codkit receipts, cache and held lock generations are disposable; submodules, special files, foreign or unowned data refuse. Both heads are retained in immutable UUID-scoped repository refs before journaling removing. Git deletes only the verified worktree roots; the registry and retained refs survive. Retry accepts an absent checkout only in removing state with no remaining Git registration and the matching preserved head. A changed preserved ref refuses. Removed is recorded after both removals and repeating removed is inert. Public CLI and full phase acceptance remain pending.
